attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his newsletter, Part II. They are not a quotation of someone else.

semantics.note: This is a firm present-tense observation with an added claim of prior anticipation. The normalised proposition keeps both parts and adds nothing.

contract.note: Marcus never defines 'tokenmaxxing' or 'clearly died'. The plain reading (a broad reversal by June 10) is ordinary and fair. Measuring through employer token-use targets is narrower than Marcus's provider/buffet framing, but it is reasonable. The anticipation part needs an earlier dated record.

evidence.note: June 5 report: Amazon, Meta and Microsoft are discouraging tokenmaxxing. That supports the direction of a retreat, but discouraging a practice does not show it broadly ended.

June 10 report: a growing number of firms are reassessing, and Walmart capped usage. This shows retrenchment that was still under way, not a completed broad end, and says nothing about the prior anticipation.

reviews.rationale: The reporting shows a real and growing retreat among major employers by June 10. It does not show that tokenmaxxing had 'clearly died' broadly; the sources frame it as an open question. The claimed earlier anticipation by Marcus and Eisman could not be verified because the interview was unreadable. No contradicting evidence. The available evidence does not meet the support condition.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his newsletter. They are not a quotation of someone else.

semantics.note: A firm two-part observation about provider and customer preferences. The normalisation is faithful; 'per-token' is a fair gloss of 'a la carte'.

contract.note: The plain reading (a broad provider retreat from generous flat-fee access plus substantial customer resistance to metering) is ordinary and fair. Marcus names no provider set or customer population, so how broad the pattern must be is decided by interpretation.

evidence.note: GitHub's own disclosure of its plan terms shows usage-based billing on all Copilot plans from June 1. That is one major service, not providers in general.

The locator says the comment was posted by gyzrich on Jun 2. In the snapshot, the quoted words appear under 'ghost' dated Jul 5, 2026, after the June 1–10 window. The item is misattributed and misdated, and it is also a single self-selected comment.

Anthropic's June 9 disclosure: a new model is included on subscriptions until June 22, then requires usage credits. This is mixed; it qualifies a blanket withdrawal but does not show all-you-can-eat access.

reviews.rationale: Only GitHub's move clearly supports the provider side, and Anthropic's staged inclusion cuts both ways. The only customer-resistance item (e2) does not match its stated author or date: the snapshot dates the quoted words July 5, outside the window. So no valid evidence of broad customer resistance by June 10 remains. Because that evidence item is not what it claims to be, I am abstaining; on the valid items alone the outcome would be unresolved.
reviews.abstain_reason: Evidence item e2 is misattributed and misdated. Its locator cites gyzrich on Jun 2, 2026, but the snapshot shows the quoted words by 'ghost' on Jul 5, 2026, after the target period.
